summary: The upload flow currently records duplicate states based on filename instead of content identity, allowing the ingestion of duplicate documents. Immediate changes are required to ensure deduplication is based on content hash to avoid data redundancy and maintain integrity.
immediate_steps: Implement checks using the computed content hash as the duplicate identity for uploads, rejecting or linking uploads with the same content hash regardless of filename before ingestion.
Reproduce the incident locally using the same failure scenario to ensure understanding of the issue.
Verify the fix against the log symptoms and selected RCA evidence.
long_term_steps: Enhance the upload system to consistently enforce content-based deduplication across all upload scenarios to eliminate duplicate entries and improve user experience.
Add input and output contract checks around the implicated code path to ensure robustness against future incidents.
Document the expected behavior and failure mode for the upload process to facilitate better understanding and quicker resolution in case of future issues.
tests_to_add: Add unit tests to validate the deduplication logic based on content hash in the upload process.
Implement integration tests to simulate user uploads with identical content and different filenames to ensure the system behaves as expected.
monitoring_improvements: Add structured logging around the implicated code path to improve traceability and understanding of issues.
Log request or trace identifiers with errors when available to facilitate rapid identification of issues.
risk_notes: There may be existing duplicate documents in the system that were ingested under the previous filename-based deduplication scheme, which could affect data reliability until cleaned up.
Users may encounter confusion regarding duplicate uploads if no user feedback mechanism is implemented before ingestion.
